statement.p: A store sells CDs at one price and DVDs at another price. The figure below shows the revenue (in dollars) of the music store as a function of the number, c, of CDs and the number, d, of DVDs that it sells. The values of the revenue are shown on each line.

p.em: (Hint: for this problem there are many possible ways to estimate the requisite values; you should be able to find information from the figure that allows you to give an answer that is essentially exact.)

li.p: What is the price of a CD? dollars
What is the price of a DVD? dollars

solution.p: The revenue function, R, is linear and so we may write it as: R = (p_1)c + (p_2)dwhere p_1 is the price of CDs and p_2 is the price of DVDs, in dollars. From the diagram, we can pick two points, such as c = 100, d=100 on the contour R=2000, and c = 100, d = 350 on the contour R = 5000. These points give the following system of linear equations: 2000 = 100 p_1 + 100 p_2, \mbox{ and } 5000 = 100 p_1 + 350 p_2.Solving gives p_1 = 8 dollars and p_2 = 12 dollars.
